The failure mode occurs when recovery time exceeds the transient window (t > 10 min), causing the decay kernel to approach zero. Thus, the mathematical unification separates mechanical crossover fatigue from generalized perceptual fatigue based strictly on the temporal structure of the applied load.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: These operators trace their lineage to Enoka and Gandevia’s foundational definitions of neuromuscular fatigue, separating peripheral muscle mechanisms from central nervous system drive. Historically, crossover fatigue was observed in static isometric paradigms (Zijdewind et al., 1998). This study extends that genealogy into dynamic, plyometric domains, proving that the temporal continuity of the stimulus dictates whether the fatigue manifests as a localized mechanical impairment or a diffuse perceptual burden.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a decision-actor perspective, a coach or athlete modeling this system must distinguish between true mechanical incapacity and perceived exhaustion. If an agent observes elevated upper-body RPE following intermittent leg work, they might erroneously veto subsequent upper-body training due to perceived systemic fatigue. However, the primitives reveal that the contralateral leg's explosive capacity remains intact. The optimal strategy involves exploiting intermittent structures to maintain mechanical readiness while managing the psychological/perceptual state space.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical anti-collinearity condition exists between the 'Contralateral Explosive Decay' and 'Intermittent Exertion Leakage' operators.
